title: The Utility of Sparse Error Detection in Quantum Simulations
authors: Henry Froland, Dorota M. Grabowska, Sebastian Grieninger, Jeremy Hartse, Anne L. Lashbrook, Zhiyao Li, Ziyuan Li, Sarah J. M. Powell, Martin J. Savage, Xiaojun Yao, Nikita A. Zemlevskiy
abstract: The recent success of error detecting codes points toward their potential application to fault-tolerant simulations of nature. In this work, we examine the utility of sparse error detection for simulating lattice gauge theories using quantum computers. In particular, we study the time evolution of the lattice Schwinger model embedded into the Iceberg code family, $[[N+2, N, 2]]$, as well as the Hypercube code family, $[[2^N, N, 2]]$. The lattice of electrons and positrons in the axial gauge is embedded into a single code block or into multiple code blocks, and this work finds that large codeblocks are advantageous in the absence of connectivity constraints. Noisy classical simulations with realistic near-term error rates, infrequent syndrome measurements and physics-aware postselection are found to improve observable estimation. Under realistic noise rates for near-term quantum computers, this work finds that sparse error detection in quantum simulations has the potential to improve accuracy of observable estimation. Additional rounds of error detection are found to systematically drive errors in observables to the noise floor set by the code. These findings suggest that incorporating minimal implementations of fault tolerance in the near-term will enhance the performance of quantum simulations in nuclear physics and high-energy physics.
summary: This paper explores using sparse error detection techniques to make quantum simulations of lattice gauge theories feasible with current, noisy quantum computers. By embedding models like the Schwinger model into specific stabilizer codes and implementing periodic syndrome measurements, the authors show that systematic error reduction can significantly boost observable accuracy. This suggests a path toward applying minimal fault tolerance in high-energy physics simulations.
main_problem: The work investigates how sparse error detection can be utilized to perform fault-tolerant quantum simulations of lattice gauge theories.
main_result: Sparse error detection shows potential for improving observable estimation accuracy in near-term quantum simulations, systematically driving errors down towards the code's noise floor.
method: The authors simulate time evolution using specific quantum error-correcting codes (Iceberg and Hypercube families) while incorporating sparse syndrome measurements and physics-aware postselection.
model_or_system: The primary model is the lattice Schwinger model, embedded into stabilizer codes like [[N+2, N, 2]] or [[2^N, N, 2]]. The simulation uses the axial gauge for Hamiltonian construction.
key_observables: Observable estimation accuracy; systematic error reduction over time; logical error rates.
important_parameters: Realistic near-term noise rates ($p_2$); codeblock size (large blocks are advantageous); number of error detection rounds.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes that incorporating minimal fault tolerance layers enhances performance, and postselection is used to eliminate leading order bit-flip errors.
paper_structure: The paper examines the utility of sparse error detection for lattice gauge theory simulations, comparing different code families and demonstrating improved accuracy under realistic noise conditions through iterative error detection rounds.
why_interesting: It directly addresses the practical challenge of running complex quantum field theory simulations on noisy near-term hardware by proposing a resource-efficient fault tolerance mechanism (sparse detection).
